analyst_view.overall: Early view: No. 2 FC Dallas host No. 7 Portland in Game 1, with a draw after 90 minutes going to penalties. Eric Quill's Dallas scored a club-record 62 goals and came from behind to beat Colorado 3-1 on Decision Day, while Marti Cifuentes's Portland arrive on four straight wins but conceded 61 in the season. Portland won 2-1 in Frisco in September and the teams drew 2-2 in Portland.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and I lean slightly higher. Both meetings this season produced goals (2-2, then a 2-1 Portland win in Frisco), Dallas have Petar Musa, who had 22 goals by late October, and Portland concede freely even while winning. A playoff opener can start slowly, but these two attacks are the stronger units on the pitch.

corners.text: The site expects 10.1 corners split evenly. I found no team news or style notes that point either way for corners, so I stay with the number; ten is a fair middle for two attacking teams.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, under 4.5. Portland knocked Dallas out of the playoffs in 2015 and 2018 and Dallas won the 2020 meeting, so there is some history, but I found nothing on discipline or the referee that pushes this either way.

shots.text: The site expects 25.4 shots, with only 11.1 for Portland. I lean higher: Portland out-created Charlotte by a wide margin in late October and have scored freely during their four-game winning run, and Dallas at home with Musa and Joaquin Valiente (13 assists) should keep their own volume up.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. I lean slightly higher in line with the goals: Portland's defence lets opponents get shots away, and Dallas's 62-goal attack is efficient, so I expect both keepers, including Portland's James Pantemis, to be busy.
